estimates.notes: Question and outcome_with_ai are null: the paper describes writing after the search task but does not establish removal or continued availability of AI or source material during writing. The reconciled screening form leaves this classification unresolved; after_ai versus with_ai/across_people is not inferred from task order alone. Timing refers to when the writers produced their advice, in the same session as the search. This is an evaluation of S3 outputs, not a new AI-assigned writer sample. The printed condition labels are retained verbatim even though the article calls the LLM-labeled proportion significantly lower than the web-link proportion and concludes that LLM advice is less helpful. The labels contradict that interpretation; condition direction requires correction or labeled choice data. Mean fields contain percentages and CI fields contain the printed proportions; no conversion was performed. The control-mean interval and the choice counts are retained in the source quotations because the supplied stats structure has no control-mean CI or choice-count fields; choice counts are not per-arm writer counts. The chi-square test assesses equality of the choice proportions including ties, not a two-condition mean difference. The test treats recipient paired choices as independent and reports no adjustment for repeated use of writer texts; se_basis is pair. within_person is null because writer assignment is between people. n_total is null because distinct randomized writers represented in the choice analysis are not enumerated; n_units is null because the total number of analyzed pairs is not explicitly printed.

open_items: AI availability during advice writing remains unconfirmed for S1-S3 and S5-S6. Sequential search and writing steps, a no-copying instruction, and a compiled survey page do not establish removal or continued availability of the source. question and outcome_with_ai are null rather than assigning after_ai or with_ai/across_people without evidence.

No outcome-level SDs or SEs, pairwise mean-difference intervals, or standardized treatment effects are printed for the extracted continuous outcomes. Demographic SDs, personal-relevance SDs, and effect sizes used for power calculations are not outcome standardizers.

Analyzed arm-level people counts are not printed for S1-S3 or S6, or for the plain-LLM and web-search arms of S5. Only the S5 links arm has an explicit analyzed people count (Supplement PDF p. 5). The S3 counts of 125 per arm on main PDF p. 8 describe texts and are not entered as people counts.

The paper does not establish the aggregation or independent observations underlying its pairwise cosine-similarity and edit-distance tests, or a correction for the reuse of writers across pairs. Degrees of freedom are not used to infer people counts or the precision unit.

S5 reports omnibus F tests for all text outcomes and pairwise t tests only for cosine similarity versus Google. Pairwise uncertainty for its other contrasts, including links versus plain LLM, is not printed. Its overall final sample cannot be assigned to any two-arm contrast.

S6 Method reports 2,129 randomized participants, exclusions of 24 and another 130, and a final sample of 1,976 (Supplement PDF p. 6); these counts are internally inconsistent. Results use F denominators of 1971 (p. 7), which also do not match the stated final sample. All printed values are retained; the outcome-specific analyzed count needs clarification.

The S3 relative-helpfulness result labels the LLM share 50.6% and the web-link share 24.6% while claiming the former is lower (main PDF p. 8). Corrected condition labels are needed. Both percentages and both printed proportion-scale confidence intervals are retained without conversion or relabeling.

S3 recipient analyses report repeated-measures tests across recipients, without accounting for repeated evaluations of the same randomized writer. The distinct writers actually represented in the rating/choice analyses and the total analyzed rating/pair counts are not printed; n_total and n_units remain null for those records. The source writer-study total is not an estimate-level analyzed count, and recipients are not added to the AI-assigned writer sample.

S3 recruitment is described only as a university behavioral lab panel; its student/general-public composition and country are not stated. Its recruited count is not explicitly identified as the count randomized (main PDF p. 7).
Model release years are not printed, and the underlying Google AI Overview model is not named. ai_tool.year is null rather than supplied from outside knowledge.

The article and supplement identify preregistrations but do not identify a preregistered primary output outcome. Primary outcome fields remain null/not_stated; S3 writer-study preregistration is not stated.

The survey section headed Experiment 1 uses the financial-scam task (Supplement PDF pp. 11-17), whereas main Experiment 1 uses vegetable gardening. The Experiment 4 instrument also refers to Replication 2/ChatGPT in its placeholders (pp. 46-47), while the main methods specify Experiment 3/Google AI Overview. Main study methods govern these mappings; instrument discrepancies remain unresolved.
S7 requires documentation of its earlier mattress-advice writer experiment before its output ratings can be attributed to an eligible randomized writer sample (Supplement PDF p. 9).
